## feature

### Joint low-MAPQ pair rescue across references and strands

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: the core requested capability. Reads with several equally good
alignments and MAPQ 0 carry no individual placement evidence, but their
joint placement can be uniquely supported; results must not depend on the
aligner's arbitrary primary picks.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. New `src/pairloom/rescue.py`. When a both-mapped template fails
   merging for a placement-level reason (`mapq_below_min`,
   `different_contig`, `orientation_incompatible`,
   `fragment_length_out_of_bounds`) and at least one mate's ORIGINAL MAPQ
   is below `--min-mapq`, both mates' exact ungapped aligned blocks are
   searched over every BAM-header contig on both strands.
2. The template relocates only when EXACTLY ONE compatible joint
   placement exists (same contig, library orientation model, fragment
   bounds) and the search is complete: neither mate's occurrence count
   exceeded `--max-candidates-per-read` and pair enumeration did not
   exhaust `--max-pair-evaluations`. Tie-breaks never count as evidence.
3. Occurrence scans are chunked at 1 Mbp fetches (bounded memory on large
   contigs) and abort early once the occurrence cap is exceeded. Strand
   labels derive from the RAW read sequence: for a reverse-strand record
   the forward probe is `revcomp(stored block)`.
4. Relocation rewrites SEQ/QUAL/CIGAR into the new alignment orientation
   (revcomp, reversed qualities, reversed CIGAR op order — clips swap
   ends), refreshes 0x10/0x20/0x2, RNEXT/PNEXT, TLEN and reciprocal MQ,
   recomputes NM/MD, removes stale scoring tags, keeps RG, sets output
   MAPQ 0, and tags `ZR:i:1`.
5. Outcomes surface as merge-rejection reasons (`rescue_applied`,
   `rescue_ambiguous`, `rescue_no_compatible_pair`,
   `rescue_search_truncated`, `rescue_unsupported_alignment`) in the
   stderr summary. `--no-rescue` disables; `--candidate-source bam` never
   rescues; templates with non-primary records and mismatch/indel mates
   are never rescued.

#### before

```text
both mates MAPQ 0, primaries on decoy contigs:
  reason different_contig (or mapq_below_min), records kept as-is;
  windowed sliding is same-contig/same-strand, so the uniquely
  supported joint placement was undiscoverable
```

#### after

```text
same template: global both-strand search -> exactly one compatible
  joint placement -> relocated to seq1, MAPQ 0, ZR:i:1, merged
  AACC 4M NM:0 MD:4; duplicate AACC copy -> rescue_ambiguous, unmerged
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
`tests/test_rescue.py` (21 tests): spec cases A/B across every valid
ambiguous primary combination (including reverse-strand primaries) merge
to `seq1 POS 1 AACC 4M NM:0 MD:4` under default parameters with both
original MAPQs 0; duplicate-AACC stays unmerged (`rescue_ambiguous`);
candidate cap and pair-evaluation budget each block uniqueness
(`rescue_search_truncated`); rf-library strand flip carries clips through
(`2S4M2S`, `NNAACCNN`); adjust-mode relocation refreshes TLEN/mate
fields; BAM-only and `--no-rescue` preserve placements; high-MAPQ
discordant pairs are never rescued.
:::

### Adjacent (zero-overlap) joining by default

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: the required joining semantics. Mates covering a continuous
fragment must join without a minimum-overlap floor, while explicit user
requirements (`--min-overlap 1`) still reject adjacency.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`--min-overlap` default changes 10 → 0; zero explicitly allows adjacent
joining. The merge walk already reconstructs the fragment reference
position by position, so adjacent mates concatenate with each base's
original quality and existing consensus rules apply wherever mates do
overlap. One uncovered base still rejects (`fragment_gap`); no base or
quality is synthesized; insertion/deletion conflict checks are unchanged.

#### before

```text
adjacent mates (overlap 0): insufficient_overlap at the default floor of 10
```

#### after

```text
--min-overlap 0 (default):  merged seq1:1 AACC 4M quals [30,31,21,22]
--min-overlap 1:            unmerged, reason insufficient_overlap (ZR set: rescue stood)
gap of one base:            unmerged, reason fragment_gap
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
`TestAdjacentJoining` pins the gap rejection, the explicit-`--min-overlap`
rejection, and config validation (0 valid, negative rejected);
`test_reference_oriented_qualities_concatenated` pins stored-orientation
quality order including reversal after a strand flip. The full existing
suite (151 → 172) stays green.
:::

## fix

None

## limitation

### Rescue pays a linear reference scan per rescued mate

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: measurable and dominant at genome scale; documented with
measured numbers and escape hatches rather than hidden.

#### description

```
type: statistic
```

Each rescued mate costs one C-speed substring scan of the reference
(chunked 1 Mbp fetches, early abort at the occurrence cap). Measured on
the 2 Mbp benchmark reference: ≈17 ms per rescue template single-threaded
(≈68 s for 4,000 both-MAPQ-0 templates). Memory stays bounded (peak RSS
unchanged at 225 MiB). Batched multi-pattern indexing is future work.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Rescue benchmark: `--pairs 20000 --ambiguous-pairs 4000 --threads 1,4`
(see the observation table).
:::

### Rescued records carry output MAPQ 0

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: deliberately conservative first implementation, blessed by the
spec; documented as policy.

#### description

```
type: text
```

A unique joint placement is real evidence, but no calibrated joint-MAPQ
model exists, so rescued records and their consensus carry MAPQ 0.
Eligibility is independent of output MAPQ.

#### evidence

```
level: unknown
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Pinned by `test_merged_record_exact_contract` (MAPQ 0, `ZR:i:1`).
:::

### Mismatch- or indel-bearing mates never rescue

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: same restriction as windowed sliding, kept deliberately so rescue
is never less conservative than the existing path.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Rescue requires both mates' original alignments to be exact and ungapped
(`rescue_unsupported_alignment` otherwise); gapped/inexact joint
re-placement is future work shared with the sliding limitation.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Exercised inside `TestDeterminism` (mutated mate →
`rescue_unsupported_alignment` path) and by the pre-existing
`test_low_mapq_excluded` behavior staying unchanged.
:::

## caveat

### Default overlap floor change accepts 1–9 bp overlaps

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: a deliberate default change with broader effect; documented so
users can restore stricter behavior explicitly.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Pairs overlapping by 1–9 bases, previously rejected as
`insufficient_overlap` at the default of 10, now merge by default. Each
such merge corroborates only a few bases; raise `--min-overlap`
explicitly for stricter evidence. The synthetic dataset's non-overlapping
pair now reports `fragment_gap` instead of `insufficient_overlap` (the
mates clear the overlap gate, then the walk meets the uncovered middle).

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
README (Consensus merging + §15 defaults), regenerated
`data/synthetic/EXPECTED.md` and expected outputs;
`test_non_overlapping_mates_kept_separate` and
`test_fragment_gap_not_synthesized` stay green.
:::

### Rescued pairs are excluded from disagreement statistics

```
level: low
```

#### reason

Low: a documented policy decision, not a silent side effect — rescued
pairs merge but never add observations.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Statistical eligibility keeps testing the ORIGINAL aligner MAPQ, which
rescue bypasses only for merging; an eligible rescue always has a
sub-threshold mate, so the disagreement population is unchanged.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
`test_rescued_pairs_do_not_add_disagreement_observations`: a rescued
overlapping pair at a position where a normal pair disagrees keeps
`dp=2` (wrongly including the rescued pair would give 4).
:::

## assumption

### Placement-level failures with a low-MAPQ mate indicate ambiguity, not chimeras

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: the trigger guard encodes this read of the biology; it is the
load-bearing assumption separating rescue from chimera masking.

#### description

```
type: text
```

Rescue fires only when at least one mate's original MAPQ is below
`--min-mapq`. High-MAPQ discordant pairs (both mates confidently placed
but incompatible) are never relocated — their discordance is treated as
evidence (structural variation, chimeras), consistent with the ordinary
path keeping their placements.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
`test_high_mapq_discordant_pair_not_rescued` pins the guard; AGENTS.md
invariant 10 records it.
:::

## observation

### Benchmark: default path, same-load A/B, and rescue cost

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: the numbers the conclusions rest on, with their measurement
context.

#### description

```
type: table
```

| Measurement | Conditions | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default run (committed RESULTS.md) | 20,000 pairs, 2 Mbp ref, load avg ≈ 4.5 | 1t 9.3 s / 2,154 pps; 2t 5.6 s; 4t 4.1 s / 4,900 pps; RSS 225–260 MiB |
| A/B pre-change (stashed) | same dataset, same load, 3 runs | 7.9 / 7.9 / 8.1 s (≈2,505 pps) |
| A/B post-change | same dataset, same load, 3 runs | 8.5 / 8.5 / 8.3 s (≈2,380 pps) |
| Rescue run, 1 thread | +4,000 both-MAPQ-0 templates | 76.1 s total (≈68 s attributable to rescue ≈ 17 ms/template) |
| Rescue run, 4 threads | same | 28.5 s; classification and reasons byte-identical to 1 thread |

The ≈5% default-path delta is adjacency working as designed: pairs with
1–9 bp overlap now run full merge walks and emit consensus records
instead of failing the cheap overlap gate. Rescue itself never fired
(all benchmark normals are MAPQ 60).

Rescue decomposition (1 thread): 2,028 templates aborted early on the
occurrence cap inside repeat islands (`rescue_search_truncated`); ~1,972
completed full scans, of which 1,004 merged and 968 rejected
`fragment_gap` (insert > 200 bp leaves uncovered middle bases).

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

## process

### Plan first; reproduce spec cases end-to-end; pin every behavior

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. Plan written before implementation; repository AGENTS.md and every
   touched module read first.
2. Spec cases A/B/duplicate/truncation reproduced through the CLI with a
   scratch script BEFORE writing tests; this caught one real defect
   early — the occurrence-search strand labels were inverted (the stored
   block of a reverse-strand record marks its REVERSE placements), which
   made case A fail and case B merge to a bogus `GGTT` placement.
3. 21 new tests cover all 12 required regression categories with
   fixture-derived exact expectations; samtools quickcheck validates
   rescued BAMs.
4. Default benchmark re-committed; a separate `--ambiguous-pairs`
   benchmark mode added and measured; same-load A/B run against the
   stashed pre-change code rather than assuming.
5. Docs updated in the same change: README (rescue section, defaults,
   policies, limitations), AGENTS.md invariants (3, 5, new 10), CLI help,
   synthetic EXPECTED.md + regenerated outputs.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

Plan: `docs/plans/20261022-102340_joint-rescue-adjacent-join.plan.qmd`;
scratch reproduction under `/tmp` (dbg scripts kept outside the repo).
